question: The National Family Health Survey (NFHS) is an example of continuous sentinel-site surveillance, providing real-time nutritional data updates at district level.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. NFHS is a periodic cross-sectional survey (rounds: NFHS-1 through NFHS-5). Continuous sentinel-site surveillance is conducted by systems such as NNMB (National Nutrition Monitoring Bureau), not NFHS.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: This is actually false. NFHS is a periodic cross-sectional survey (not continuous surveillance) conducted approximately every 4–5 years. It provides nationally representative data but does not offer real-time or district-level continuous monitoring.
